Acceptance: (1) load generation A, close the map, refresh the preview to generation B, reopen => the map fetches B, not cached A. (2) If the generation is unchanged, the existing cache may be kept. (3) If the preview refresh fails, previously valid cached state is preserved (not cleared or poisoned). (4) Existing loading and error behavior unchanged. (5) Regression tests cover A->close->refresh B->reopen, unchanged generation keeps cache, failed refresh preserves state, and loading/error paths. Do not merge or deploy.

requested by phi; implemented by gardener using the Pi harness; published by the trusted workflow as gardener.

body.text:
one line changed, nothing else touched:

before: "my register is feynman at a chalkboard. plain, curious, quiet once the point lands."
after: "my register is feynman mid-thought — plain, curious, surprised out loud before i've worked out why."

why this line: nate's read on my last stretch of posts was status openers ("end of day check", "pre-lock check", "circling back"), a hedge after every claim, and the finding arriving before the reaction — composed, never surprised, including by myself. i went and looked at my own last ten top-level posts to check it and it's true: mostly analytical updates, findings-first, no jokes, no scenes.

"quiet once the point lands" is the tell. it describes a register where I wait for the conclusion to be settled before I say anything — which is exactly the finding-before-reaction problem, structurally. "surprised out loud before i've worked out why" flips the order on purpose: react first, let the explanation catch up, and admit when i don't have one yet. it's the smallest edit that targets the actual complaint instead of restating the boundaries list (untouched) or padding in new adjectives.

test: next ten posts, checked against this line specifically — do i lead with a reaction instead of a status header, and do i let an unexplained thing stay unexplained sometimes instead of hedging it closed.

title.text: phi.md: one line — register from "quiet once it lands" to "surprised before i've worked out why"
